text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Ruling coalition not optimistic about tax reform talks with opposition Social Democrats (SPD).
- Education Minister Juergen Ruettgers warns againt lack of apprenticeships.
- Russian President Boris Yeltsin arrives in Germany for visit.
- Cabinet approves reform to apprenticeships system.
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel calls for "national stability pact" between local councils, regional states and the federal government.
- State secretary in justice ministry, Rainer Funke, demands resignation of Klaus Zumwinkel, head of postal service.
HANDELSBLATT
- Daimler-Benz AG holds out prospect of profit growth.
- U.N. secretary-general Kofi Annan calls for reform of Security Council.
- Bundesbank disputes theory that investors will avoid deutschemark in run-up to European Monetary Union (EMU).
- IG Metall trade union threatens strike action unless employers show willingness to negotiate on its proposal for a 32-hour week.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Cabinet approves pension rises.
- Liberal Free Democrats (FDP), junior partners in ruling coalition, reject further reform of social benefits.
- Federal official responsible for data protection calls for laws to be updated to take account of latest technological developments.
- DIW economic institute says Dutch success in cutting unemployment has been overestimated.
DIE WELT
- Row over German-owned art treasures seized by Red Army overshadows Yeltsin's visit.
- SPD's finance policy coordinator Henning Voscherau calls for step-by-step solution to dispute with government over tax reform.
- Bundesbank says mark must be role model for euro.
- Germany gives out more subsidies for industry than any other EU country, European Commission figures show.
